docs.title: MUST HAVE
docs.text:
Deducción lógica sobre algo que ha sucedido en el pasado

  • He didn't hear any voice. The thief must have gone.
  • The kitchen was clean. They must have gone to have lunch out.

docs.title: CAN'T HAVE
docs.text:
Deducción sobre algo que no pasó en el pasado basado en las evidencias del presente.

  • He can't have got the job.
  • She can't have passed such a difficult exam.

docs.title: MIGHT/MAY/COULD HAVE
docs.text:
Expresa posibilidad en el pasado

  • He didn't even know how to program. They couldn't have given him the job.
  • The little girl may have lost her keys
  • Our neighbors might have heard some noises when our car was stolen

docs.title: COULD HAVE
docs.text: Posibilidad en el pasado pero no se llevó a cabo. ahora es tarde. - She could have called the doctor early in the morning. - You could have been a good doctor, but you decided to study engineering.

docs.title: SHOULD HAVE || OUGHT TO HAVE
docs.text: Algo deseable en el pasado (opinión) pero ahora es tarde Deber u obligación incumplido - He should have taken some advice from his friend but he didn't - She should have adked you before borrowing your pen - Paul ought to have waited until the lights were green before he crossed the street, but he didn't wait.

docs.title: SHOULDN'T HAVE
docs.text:
Arrepentimiento sobre hecho pasado. Tuvo lugar pero no era deseable.

  • They shouldn't have gone out late last night, but they did.
  • She shouldn't have taken the matter too seriously.

docs.title: NEEDN'T HAVE
docs.text: Algo se hizo pero no era necesario. - When the party was over, I realized that you needn't have cooked so much food as most of it was untouched.

docs.title: WOULD HAVE
docs.text: En el Tercer condicional (Condición irreal del pasado que habría determinado otra del pasado) - If my parents had had more money, I would have gone to university. Y en el mixto 2+3 (Condición irreal del presente que determina una del pasado) - If I were rich, I would have bought that expensive car.

docs.title: 2º Condicional
docs.text: (Condición irreal del presente que determina una del presente) - If I were rich, I would spend my life travelling Y en el mixto 3 + 2 (Condición irreal del pasado que determina una del presente) - If I had studied harder, I would find a good job. (now)

docs.title: WISH
docs.text: • Expresa deseos quejas y lamentos

docs.title: En el presente: WISH + PRON + PAST SIMPLE
docs.text:
• It's raining! I wish I had an umbrella
  • I wish I lived here
  • Do you ever wish you could fly? Puede usarse were
  • I wish I were in Scotland
  • I wish she were here now.

docs.text:
• I wish I had never born
  • I wish I had never say that
  • I wish I had known that Gary was ill
  • I wish we hadn't gone to bed so late last night
  • I wish I had seen him
  • Do you wish you'd studied science instead of language?
  • I wish I could have gone

docs.title: En el futuro: WISH + PRON + COULD / WOULD  + INF
docs.text:
• I wish I could relearn to drive.
  • I wish I would stop raining
  • I wish you could stay longer
  • I with it would stop raining
  • I wish somebody would answer it
  • I wish your wouldn't keep interrupting me

No lo confundas con el: - Me gustaría: > I would like to relearn to drive.

Si acaba en t y d --> /id/ Si es sorda: k, ch, sh, p, s, f, x, th. --> /t/ Si lo demas /d/ +

💡 Diferencia con “used to” o “would”:

  1. Past simple: “We had breakfast together every morning.”

    • Simplemente relata lo que pasaba en el pasado, puede ser un hecho o rutina.

  2. Used to: “We used to have breakfast together every morning.”

    • Enfatiza que ya no lo hacemos, hábito pasado.

  3. Would: “We would have breakfast together every morning.”

    • También indica hábito pasado, más literario o narrativo.

En resumen:

  • Past simple → rutina pasada sin comentar si sigue o no.

  • Used to / would → hábito pasado que ya no ocurre (o narrativo).

docs.title: Advices
docs.text:
En inglés, cuando una palabra funciona como modificador (por ejemplo, un sustantivo que describe a otro sustantivo), normalmente se usa en singular, aunque se hable de algo plural.

Por eso se dice: - question formation (formación de preguntas) - car park (estacionamiento de coches, no cars park) - shoe store (tienda de zapatos, no shoes store) - toothbrush (cepillo de dientes, no teethbrush)

docs.title: Preposiciones lugar: In vs To
docs.text:
“to” → dirección / movimiento hacia un lugar - Se usa cuando hablamos de ir a un lugar, sin implicar necesariamente que permanecemos allí.

“in” → dentro de un lugar, indicando ubicación / residencia / permanencia - Se usa cuando algo o alguien está dentro de un lugar, es decir, se encuentra allí. Se centra en estar en un sitio.

I haven't lived in Toledo. I only went to Toledo for a holiday last year.

docs.title: For vs To
docs.text:
"To" primarily indicates: - Purpose or intention (propósito o intención). Con to-. Finalidad concreta de la acción específica. - I study hard to pass the exam. - Direction or movement toward a destination (dirección / movimiento hacia un lugar) - We are going to the park. - The recipient of an action (destinatario de una acción) - Giving - I gave the book to my friend. - A range or limit (rango o límite) - The temperature rose to 30°C. - It's a quarter to two - Comparing - I prefer playing football to working

"For" primarily indicates: - Purpose or function (propósito o función). Con -ing. Propósito general. Función o uso de algo. - We stopped for petrol. - Benefit or advantage (beneficio / ventaja) - Exercise is good for your health. - Duration or period of time (duración o período de tiempo) - I have lived here for five years. - Representation or support (representación o apoyo) - The union provides support for its members. - Schedule - I made an appointment for April 2026 - Agree with - Are you for or against this situation?

"Para..."

For + Noun To + Verb - We stopped for petrol- I had to run for the bus - We stopped to get petrol- I had to run to catch the bus

To (To + verb) - Indica la finalidad concreta de algo - Do you have much work to do? - It's hard to find a place to park in the city centre - Would you like something to eat - Puede tener una preposición después del verbo - I need something to open this bottle with

for somebody to do something (para alguien para hacer algo) - There weren't any chairs for us to sit on, so we sat on the floow.

for (do)ing (para dar definición general, decir que algo se usa para) - This brush is for washing the dishes

Para destacar la finalidad usar to-. Nunca se usa for -ing en ese caso - I went into the kitchen to wash the dishes

Usar What ...for para preguntar por el propósito - What is this switch for? - What did you do that for?

so that so Se usa so that (no se usa to) con can/could y will/would

  • She's learning English so that she can study in Canada
  • We moved to London so that we could see our friends more often
  • I hurried so that I wouldn't be late

También se puede omitir el that. - I hurried so I wouldn't be late.

enough/too for y enough/too to

Recuerda que el orden es: too + adj y adj + enough

Se usa for para alguien/alguna cosa y to para hacer algo - Thi bag isn't big enought for all my clotes - That shirt is too small for you - She's not enough to have a driving license - The bridge is** just wide enough** for two cars to pass one another.

docs.title: Question formation
docs.text: There are two types of questions:

docs.title: Yes-No Question
docs.text:
• Se responden con patrón de sí-no
  • Siguen la estructura: Auxiliary Verb / Modal Verb + Sujeto + Main Verb ?
  • Se responden con short answers.
Question Short Answer Long Answer Are you studying English? Yes, I’m | No, I’m not Yes, I am studying English | No, I am not studying English Is she happy? Yes, she’s | No, she isn’t Yes, she is happy | No, she is not happy Do you like pizza? Yes, I do | No, I don’t Yes, I like pizza | No, I don’t like pizza Did he call you? Yes, he did | No, he didn’t Yes, he called me | No, he didn’t call me Will they come? Yes, they will | No, they won’t Yes, they will come | No, they will not come Can she swim? Yes, she can | No, she can’t Yes, she can swim | No, she can’t swim Should they study more? Yes, they should | No, they shouldn’t Yes, they should study more | No, they shouldn’t study more Might he come tomorrow? Yes, he might | No, he might not Yes, he might come tomorrow | No, he might not come tomorrow

docs.title: Wh-Questions
docs.text:
• Contienen una question word (When, Where, Who, Why, What, How, How much-many, How often)

  • Siguen la estructura: Question Word + Auxiliary Verb / Modal Verb + Suj + Main verb ?

  • Se pueden usar negative questions para expresar sorpresa ante algo inesperado o para verificar algo que se cree cierto. 

    Examples:
- Can't you swim? Yes, I can (Sí, puede nadar)
- Aren't you tired? Yes, I am  (Sí, estoy cansado)
- Haven't you done your homework? Yes, I have (Sí, la he hecho)
- Isn't it amazing? Yes, I it is (Sí, lo es)
- Isn't this a beautiful place? Yes, it is (Sí, lo es)

  • Si el verbo viene normalmente seguido de una preposición, la preposición va al final de la oración. - What are you thinking about? - Who does this bag belong to? A menudo solo se usa la question word + preposición - What about?

A: I’m worried about something.  
B (larga): What are you thinking about?  
B (corta): About what?

A: I saw her yesterday, and she looked strange.  
B (larga): Who were you looking at?  
B (corta): Who at?

A: I was talking to someone on the phone.  
B (larga): Who were you talking to?  
B (corta): Who to?

A: I’ve been standing here for ages.  
B (larga): Who are you waiting for?  
B (corta): Who for?

A: I don’t really agree with him.  
B (larga): Who do you agree with?  
B (corta): Who with?

A: It depends on the weather.  
B (larga): What does it depend on?  
B (corta): What on?

  • Cuando la question word es el sujeto de la pregunta en present o past simple no se usa do/did. > En definitiva, si vamos a responder con un sujeto, no se pone.

    Example: Who wrotes Shakespeare? - William Shakespeare wrote him. ← formal y completa - William Shakespeare. ← suficiente en conversación

    Example: Who lives in that house? - Sheriff Wiggum - Sheriff Wiggum lives there

WHO
Who called you yesterday?  
→ John did.  ← “Who” es el sujeto
Who did you call yesterday?  
→ I called John.  ← “Who” es el objeto

WHAT
What made that noise?  
→ The wind did.  ← “What” es el sujeto
What did you make yesterday?  
→ I made a cake.  ← “What” es el objeto

WHICH
Which of these books belongs to you?  
→ This one does.  ← “Which” es el sujeto
Which book did you buy?  
→ I bought this one.  ← “Which” es el objeto

WHOSE
Whose idea won the contest?  
→ Maria’s did.  ← “Whose idea” es el sujeto
Whose book did you borrow?  
→ I borrowed John’s.  ← “Whose book” es el objeto

WHERE
Where is happening the meeting?  ← Muy formal / raro  
Where did you go yesterday?  
→ I went to the park.  ← “Where” es el objeto de “go”

WHEN, WHY, HOW
When did you arrive?  
→ I arrived at 8.  ← “When” no es sujeto
Why did she leave early?  
→ She left because she was tired.  ← “Why” no es sujeto
How did you solve the problem?  
→ I solved it with patience.  ← “How” no es sujeto

docs.text:

  • Siguen el orden sujeto + verbo y no se usa do-does/did en la segunda parte de la pregunta. Se puede usar if/wether si es una yes-no question.

docs.title: Usos del comparativo
docs.text:
• Suele ir seguido con than y un pronombre o nombre.: I think that she's more intelligent than her sister.

  • Cualificados por palabras y frases como as much, a lot, far, a bit / little, slightly: You should go by train, it would be much cheaper. Could you be a bit quieter? I'm feeling a lot better. Do yoyu have one that's slightly biggest?

  • Pueden ser contrastados. Un cambio en una cualidad provoca un cambio en la otra.

    • The smaller the gift, the easier it is to send
    • The more stressed you are, the worse it is for your health.

  • Los comparativos pueden ser enlazados con and para mostrar un incremento continuo de una cualidad particular

    • The sea was getting rougher and rougher
    • Her illness was becoming worse and worse
    • He became more and more tired as the weeks went by.

docs.title: Usos del superlativo
docs.text:
• También pueden ser colocados antes de nombres en la posición de atributo o después del verbo to be y otros verbos de enlace

    • The most delicious chocolate cake I' ve ever eaten
    • Annabel was the youngest
    • This restaurant is the best

  • A menudo son usados por sí solos si queda claro qué o quién es comparado. Si se quiere especificar puede ponerse un nombre o una frase comenzando por in o of

    • Annabel was the youngest child
    • Annabel was the youngest of the children
    • This restauran is the best in town

    • She was the least intelligent of the three sisters.

docs.title: Mantener opciones abiertas 🔓
docs.text:
• To keep one's options open → 🚪 Dejar la puerta abierta a más posibilidades

She weighed up her options before choosing a university. He weighed up his options before deciding to move abroad. We need to weigh up all the options before making a final decision.

I gave it a lot of thoughts before replying to her message. He gave it a lot of thoughts before quitting his job. She gave it a lot of thoughts and finally decided to travel alone.

You should take into consideration the costs before buying a new car. We took into consideration all possible risks before starting the project. She took into consideration her friends’ advice before making a decision.

I’m in two minds about moving to a new city. She was in two minds about accepting the job offer. He’s in two minds about buying a new phone.

I can’t make up my mind which dress to buy. She finally made up her mind and accepted the offer. He made up his mind to start exercising every morning.

Don’t make a rush decision; think it through. He made a rush decision and bought the first car he saw. They made a rush decision to move without checking the rent.

I was going to go out, but I changed my mind. She changed her mind about moving abroad. He changed his mind after talking with his friends.

I’m having second thoughts about quitting my job. She had second thoughts after signing the contract. They had second thoughts about moving to another country.

I have a hunch that it’s going to rain today. She had a hunch something was wrong. He had a hunch the team would win the match.

I went with my gut feelings and chose the red dress. She went with her gut feelings and trusted him. He went with his gut feelings and invested in the company.

I can’t put my finger on what’s causing the problem. She finally put her finger on the reason for the delay. He put his finger on the issue that everyone had missed.

I’m keeping my options open until I get a better offer. She decided to keep her options open before committing. He’s keeping his options open in case something better comes along.

docs.title: quite, pretty, rather and fairly
docs.text:
quite y pretty son menos que "very" pero más que "a little"

quite: Va antes de a/an + adj. pretty: Va después de a/an + adj y se usa en Inglés informal

Sarah has quite a good job. Sarah 
Sarah has a pretty good job.

quite, quite a lot of puede usarse también sin adjetivo, solo con un nombre - It was quite a surprise (big surprise) - There were quite a lot of guests at the wedding

quite + V - I quite like tennis, but it's not my favourite sport. (Me gusta bastante el tennis)

docs.title: 1.  AI Advantages and Disadvantages
docs.text:
AI (Artificial Intelligence) is a branch of computer science which aims to develop intelligent systems, that is, systems that perform tasks humans normally do. They're systems that can learn, think, make decisions, research...

Some advantages are: - AI allows to do repetitive /ripetitif/ tasks that we don't want to do. For example, I usually use AI at work when I need a piece of code that I know how to write but I don't feel like typing. I can ask it to do it and it does it for me. - AI allows us to get fast answers without needing to look for them on Google. - AI allows me to learn about a lot of topics I'm interested in like history, technology, science, travels, etc...

Some disadvantages are: - In my opinion, AI could cause job losses and increase unemployment in the future - AI could make mistakes. This phenomenom is known as hallutinations. We can't expect that the AI results to be determinitics. AI results is obtained with a high influence of probability. - Energy consumption. Using AI requires an enormous energy consumption. - Security problems. If we rely on AI for all our systems, I think that we could suffer security problems in the future.

/ei ai/

docs.title: 2.  Importance of English
docs.text:
Well, I consider English to be absolutely important. 

First, English’s important because it’s the most spoken second language. I think if you can speak English, you can communicate with people all over the world. For example, even if you live in India and I live in Spain, we’re talking now thanks to English. 

Second, English’s important because it allows you to access a lot of knowledge and information. For example, when I need to look for something on the Internet, I’m more likely to find it if I search in English. 

Third, we can use English for entertainment. Many sitcoms, movies, and TV shows are in English. 

Also, English increases opportunities to get a better job and a higher salary. In most of the job offers I see, English is a required skill.
